evidence.quote: praeter Bedae excerpta et codicem Abrincensem interpolatum scripta editaque exemplaria omnia redeunt fere ad unum codicem Londiniensem Cottonianum
cum et archetypum fuerit eius qui sequitur [D] et primis duobus editoribus P et Q pro textus fundamento
intelleget tribus libris interpolatis subesse archetypum interpolatum et ipsum, sed modeste

texts.notes: C is stated to be the exemplar of D (D descriptus), so the C branch has effectively one independent witness; the interpolated branch is A, X and the lost source used by Polydore (P). P is an early edition mixing C with that lost interpolated codex. The editor never names a common archetype above C and the A-X-P archetype explicitly; the two-way split is implied by 'omnia redeunt ad C' except A (and X/P).

evidence.quote: Primi tertiique ordinis libri cum a computatione incipiant perducta ad a. 891 ... computum eum praeposuit librarius is ad quem tam anonymi codices redeunt quam Gildani
itaque primae tertiaeque classis archetypo communi forma data est a. 891
hinc colligemus reliquarum familiarum principes proxime quidem accessisse ad primae classis archetypum, sed ex hoc ipso nequaquam descendere
Secunda familia ipsa bipertita est, repraesentata scilicet cum codice ... Carnutino Z ... tum duobus libris ... M, et ... N
librarius archetypi eius, a quo MN descendunt, praeter codicem Carnutini similem adhibuit alterum familiae Gildanae
Tertium ordinem libri constituunt numero multi corpus de quo agitur proponentes sub nomine Gildae ... P ... Q ... D
Codicem a Nennio adhibitum esse ordinis primi vel inde colligitur

texts.notes: Mommsen names three orders: I anonymi (HK), II Gallica/Marcian (Z; MN), III Gildan (PQD). He says I and III share a scribe/archetype dated by the 891 computus, which is the basis for the recorded 2-way top; he could also be read as giving three coordinate orders (k=3), so check this. The Nennian recension (C, D2; copies L of C, G of D) is said to come from an order-I codex near K, but its Latin witnesses also share errors with the Gildan order. MN are contaminated from the Gildan family. Sections differ in which witnesses carry them; codices 1-11 collated only for c. 7-10 are omitted.
